function: p. 9: MADDPG learns UAV transmit power and bandwidth allocation jointly with 3D trajectory for UAV-GT links; FL-trained ANN refines sensed GT locations (positioning, digital FedAvg).
system: p. 4, 9-10: 3 rotary-wing UAVs, 8 mobile ground terminals, 0.2x0.2 km; urban air-to-ground LoS-probability channel; antenna arrays not specified; Table I: B=2 GHz as printed, P_max=5 mW.
method: p. 6-10: supervised FedAvg-trained ANN for GT location with game-theoretic data-volume rule (PR); MADDPG reinforcement learning (centralized training, distributed execution) for trajectory, bandwidth, power.
data_channel: p. 4-6: simulated urban air-to-ground LoS-probability path-loss channel [46]; ANN training data generated by simulation (ISAC range measurements, GPS ground truth); no dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 8-11: FL model tested on pooled local samples of all UAVs; MADDPG compared in Scenarios I-IV (undefined; 3 UAVs, 8 GTs); FL loss versus UAV count.
baselines: p. 10: MADDPG-ISAC-NoPR (no data adjustment), MADDPG without ISAC, DDPG-ISAC, DDPG; FL without PR; all learned variants, no non-learned or classical baseline.
metrics: p. 10-13: maximum UAV energy (J), communication data rate (Mbps), FL training loss, training energy, communication overhead, Q-value.
complexity: none; only modeled training energy (p. 6, Fig. 4) and ANN layer sizes 5-64-128-64-2 (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "considering an urban environment, the LoS probability of a UAV-GT link is given by" an analytical air-to-ground model (Table I, p. 10, cites [46]); p. 6: "we directly simulates the generation of training data". Custom simulation; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 8: "The resulting global model is then evaluated using a test dataset composed by combining samples from the local datasets of all UAVs." This is pooled data of the same simulation; Scenarios I-IV are never defined and no trained model is stated to be tested in an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "we adopt a hierarchical ablation experiment design" and "we remove the PR strategy and compare MADDPG-ISAC-NoPR with MADDPG-ISAC"; Table II compares only MADDPG and DDPG variants. No non-learned optimization or heuristic baseline is run (convex optimization on p. 2 and grid search on p. 5 are only motivation).
q4_support: p. 6: "the local training energy consumption of each participating UAV in one round of global iteration is" a modeled energy (Eq. 12, Fig. 4); p. 13 only says "higher training complexity" qualitatively. No complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
q5_support: p. 6: "we directly simulates the generation of training data" shows synthetic data; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere (the only URL is the IEEE rights notice, p. 1).
notes: Included under area 6: the MADDPG learns UAV transmit power and bandwidth allocation (physical layer in aerial links) jointly with 3D trajectory (p. 9, Eq. 23), so above_phy does not apply; NTN (6) outranks ISAC (5) and single-antenna links are admitted for NTN. The FL-trained ANN only refines GT locations (positioning) and aggregates digitally with FedAvg (p. 8), so it is not area 7. The channel is an urban air-to-ground LoS-probability model with parameters from [46] (Table I, p. 10), analytical and not standardized, so q1 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. q4 is 0 because only modeled training energy is reported.
